# Diagnostic investigations and procedures in urology

*Categories: Clinical knowledge > Urology > Basics of urology > Diagnostic investigations and procedures in urology*

[Original Article Link](/library/c50aQg)

---

## Summary

Patients with urological symptoms are diagnosed using clinical evaluation and diagnostic studies. <u>Urodynamic studies</u> are used to evaluate functional and anatomical abnormalities of the <u>lower urinary tract</u> and commonly include <u>cystometry</u>, <u>uroflowmetry</u>, <u>urethral pressure profile</u>, and <u>leak point pressure</u>. Imaging studies (e.g., <u>ultrasound</u>, CT, <u>MRI</u>) may be used to evaluate for <u>urinary tract</u> abnormalities based on clinical suspicion. <u>Cystoscopy</u> provides direct visualization of the <u>urethra</u>, <u>bladder</u>, and urethral orifices. <u>Urinary drainage procedures</u> include <u>transurethral catheterization</u>, <u>suprapubic catheterization</u>, <u>percutaneous nephrostomy</u>, and <u>ureteral stenting</u>.




See also “<u>Diagnostic evaluation of the kidney and urinary tract</u>.”

---

## Urodynamic studies

<u>Urodynamic studies</u> use the characteristics of urinary flow (pressure and flow rate at various points during <u>micturition</u> and at rest) to evaluate the functional and anatomical abnormalities of the <u>lower urinary tract</u>.




### Cystometry




* Description

* Assesses <u>bladder</u> pressure during filling

* Determines <u>detrusor</u> and <u>bladder</u> function (activity, sensation, capacity, and compliance)

* Indications

* To differentiate between <u>detrusor</u> overactivity and <u>stress incontinence</u>

* To determine neurological abnormalities of the <u>bladder</u> (e.g., <u>hypotonic bladder</u>)

* Procedure

* <u>Bladder</u> is filled with water through a urethral catheter at a steady rate

* The vesical pressure is measured through this urethral catheter, while the <u>intraabdominal pressure</u> is measured via a vaginal or rectal pressure catheter

* The <u>detrusor</u> pressure is the difference in pressure between these two catheters





### Uroflowmetry




* Description: : an objective, noninvasive test used in the evaluation of patients with suspected <u>bladder outlet obstruction</u>

* Indications

* <u>Outlet obstruction</u> (e.g., <u>benign prostatic hypertrophy</u>, urethral overactivity, <u>urethral stricture</u> following <u>surgery</u>)

* Weak <u>detrusor</u> (e.g., <u>hypotonic bladder</u>)

* Increased Valsalva during voiding

* Procedure

* Patient is asked to void into a funnel that measures the volume and rate of urine flow.

* Measures the volume of urine voided over time

* Interpretation 

* Normal: a continuous, single bell-shaped curve with urine volume > 200 mL (over 15–30 seconds) and at a rate > 15 mL per second

* Abnormal: an abnormal curve or urine volume at a rate < 15 mL per second 

* Bell-shaped with a flattened curve: indicates obstruction (most likely due to <u>benign prostatic hypertrophy</u>)

* Rapid rise followed by a plateau: indicates obstruction (most likely due to <u>urethral stricture</u>)

* Irregular, undulating, wavy: indicates <u>bladder sphincter dyssynergia</u>





![Uroflowmetry](media/klabz55qz9eu71imj3t0cio5.jpg)

Uroflowmetry




### Pressure-flow study [[1]](/library/Nza-GM)




* Description

* To determine the underlying mechanism of an abnormal <u>uroflowmetry</u> assessment

* Measures <u>detrusor</u> pressure while voiding

* Indications

* Increased Valsalva during voiding

* Weak <u>detrusor</u> (e.g., <u>hypotonic bladder</u>)

* <u>Outlet obstruction</u> (e.g., <u>benign prostatic hypertrophy</u>, urethral overactivity, <u>urethral stricture</u> following <u>surgery</u>)





### Urethral pressure profile




* Description

* Assesses intrinsic sphincter function

* Measures the intraluminal urethral integrity at different pressures (filling and voiding pressures are measured under different types of provocation, e.g., <u>Valsalva maneuver</u>, <u>coughing</u>)

* Indications

* Sphincter dysfunction (e.g., due to <u>multiparity</u>, low <u>estrogen</u> levels)

* Urinary <u>stress incontinence</u>

* Procedure: A specialized urethral catheter, mounted with microtransducers, is withdrawn at a slow and steady rate from the <u>bladder</u> until it exits the <u>external urethral meatus</u>.





### Leak point pressure




* Description

* Assesses intrinsic sphincter function (but during dynamic testing, unlike <u>urethral pressure profile</u> testing)

* Determines the intravesical pressure required to produce urine leakage in the presence of increased abdominal pressure (i.e., during <u>Valsalva maneuver</u>) and the absence of <u>detrusor</u> contraction

* May be performed during <u>cystometry</u>

* Indications

* Sphincter dysfunction (e.g., due to <u>multiparity</u>, low <u>estrogen</u> levels)

* Urinary <u>stress incontinence</u>





### Postvoid residual volume (<u>PVR</u>)




* Description: measures the volume of urine that remains in the <u>bladder</u> after voiding

* Indications

* <u>Bladder outlet obstruction</u>

* Weak <u>detrusor</u>

* Procedure: : may be performed using straight catheterization or <u>ultrasound</u> of the <u>bladder</u>

* Interpretation: <u>PVR</u> < 100 mL is usually considered normal.  [[2]](/library/hRdc5p0)[[3]](/library/SkdyMJ0)





### <u>EMG</u>




* Description: a procedure that studies the electrical potentials of depolarized muscle, specifically the neural pathways involved in <u>micturition</u> (by evaluating the segment of the sacral spinal cord involved)

* Indication: to determine neurological abnormalities of the <u>bladder</u> (e.g., <u>hypotonic bladder</u>)

* Procedure: Electrodes or a concentric needle are inserted into the <u>urethral sphincter</u>.





References:[[4]](/library/qpaCql)[[5]](/library/lzavGM)[[6]](/library/mzaVtM)[[6]](/library/mzaVtM)

## Imaging techniques

### <u>Ultrasound</u>



* Indications

* Renal: visualization of renal tumors, <u>renal cysts</u>, <u>nephrolithiasis</u>, and <u>hydronephrosis</u> (see also “<u>Renal POCUS</u>”)

* <u>Bladder</u>: to evaluate for <u>bladder</u> wall thickening, <u>bladder calculi</u>, tumors, <u>urinary retention</u> (see also “<u>Bladder POCUS</u>”)

* <u>Prostate</u>;  : to estimate <u>prostate</u> volume, shape, <u>echogenicity</u>, and evaluate for <u>prostatic abscesses</u> or masses

* Scrotal and penile: to evaluate for <u>testicular torsion</u>, <u>cryptorchidism</u>, trauma, <u>testicular tumors</u>, <u>varicocele</u>, and <u>epididymitis</u>

### CT



* Indications

* Investigation of choice to detect <u>urinary calculi</u> and renal masses

* Visualization of the <u>urothelium</u> in suspected malignancies and cases of obstruction

* <u>CT angiography</u> helps evaluate acute <u>pelvic</u> trauma and <u>tumor</u> blood supply, as well as diagnose renal vascular <u>malformations</u>.




### <u>MRI</u>



* Indications

* To differentiate between <u>renal cysts</u> and <u>neoplasms</u>

* For accurate staging of <u>bladder</u> and <u>prostate cancers</u>

* As an alternative to contrast CT in patients who are allergic to <u>iodine</u>-based radiocontrast




### Renal scintigraphy




* Description: : a diagnostic procedure in which radioisotopes are used to assess the anatomy and function of the <u>kidneys</u>

* Indications

* Assessment for renal scarring (usually caused by reflux) and significant <u>urinary obstruction</u>

* Estimation of <u>differential renal function</u>

* Screening for <u>renal artery stenosis</u>

* Monitoring of <u>renal transplants</u>

* Procedure: IV administration of <u>technetium</u> (<u>Tc-99m</u> pertechnetate/gamma emitter) and measurement of its distribution in the body with a gamma camera

* Static renal scintigraphy: a diagnostic test in which a radiotracer that is retained by the <u>renal cortex</u> is used to assess renal function as well as the degree of structural damage to the <u>renal cortex</u>

* Injection of Tc-99m DMSA (<u>Tc-99m</u> <u>dimercaptosuccinic acid</u>; an injectable radioactive gamma-emitter dye that rapidly accumulates in the renal <u>parenchyma</u> and very small amounts are eliminated from the <u>kidney</u>)

* Imaging is performed ∼ 3 hours after injection, when the dye has reached the <u>kidneys</u> for <u>renal clearance</u>.

* Dynamic renal scintigraphy: a diagnostic test in which a radiotracer that is excreted by the <u>kidney</u> is used to assess renal <u>perfusion</u> as well as urine flow in the <u>urinary tract</u>

* Injection of Tc-99m MAG3 (mercaptoacetyltriglycine; a form of injectable <u>technetium</u> that rapidly accumulates in the renal <u>parenchyma</u> and is cleared almost exclusively by tubular excretion)

* Serial imaging from the time of injection until the end of the procedure (up to 30 minutes)





### Voiding cystourethrography [[7]](/library/KRdULp0)[[8]](/library/6RdjLp0)




* Description: a diagnostic procedure used to determine the presence and severity of <u>vesicoureteral reflux</u> and detect anatomical abnormalities

* Indications [[9]](/library/Z51Zih0)

* Abnormal <u>ultrasound</u> findings, e.g.:

* <u>Vesicoureteral reflux</u>

* <u>Urinary tract obstruction</u> (e.g., <u>hydronephrosis</u>, <u>hydroureter</u>)

* <u>Recurrent UTIs</u>

* Suspected <u>urethral stricture</u>

* Trauma

* Contraindications

* <u>UTI</u>

* Contrast <u>allergy</u>

* Procedure

* Radiocontrast dye is injected into the <u>bladder</u> using a urinary catheter (retrograde filling of the <u>bladder</u> with contrast).

* <u>Fluoroscopy</u> is performed during voiding.

* Increased <u>bladder</u> pressure during voiding may reveal previously undetected reflux. [[10]](/library/KbbUuH)

* Complication: <u>UTI</u>

### Intravenous urography [[11]](/library/JzasFM)




* Description: a diagnostic procedure that involves intravenous contrast agent and <u>x-rays</u> to provide images of the genitourinary tract

* Indication: visualization of <u>renal excretion</u> and the course of the <u>ureters</u>

* Procedure

* Contrast dye is injected intravenously.

* Serial <u>pelvic</u> <u>x-rays</u> (taken at specific time intervals) help assess the <u>kidneys</u>, <u>ureters</u>, <u>bladder</u>, and <u>urethra</u>.

* Contraindications

* <u>Hyperthyroidism</u>

* <u>Renal insufficiency</u>

* Contrast medium <u>allergy</u>

* <u>Multiple myeloma</u>

### CT urography




* Description: an imaging study that uses CT with intravenous contrast to assess the anatomy and, to a certain degree, function of the urinary collecting system, renal calyces, <u>ureters</u>, and <u>bladder</u>

* Indications: a first-line imaging test to assess for genitourinary abnormalities (e.g., <u>malignancy</u>, stricture)

* Procedure: CT with contrast dye injected intravenously





![Bladder mass](media/cp9ejfty1upj2y42xs0fqjjs.jpg)

Bladder mass




### Retrograde urethrography [[12]](/library/3wYSir)




* Description: : a diagnostic test in which contrast agent is injected into the <u>urethra</u> to evaluate for <u>urethral injuries</u> and disorders via <u>x-ray</u>

* Indications: suspected anatomical and/or functional urethral lesions, e.g.:

* <u>Urethral strictures</u>

* <u>Urethral injuries</u>

* Urethral <u>fistulas</u>

* Contraindications

* <u>UTI</u>

* Contrast <u>allergy</u>

* Procedure
1. * Insert a small catheter (e.g., 8 Fr <u>Foley catheter</u>) into the <u>urethra</u>.
2. * Slowly inflate the balloon to enable a snug fit.
3. * Slowly inject contrast material into the <u>urethra</u>.
4. * Obtain <u>x-rays</u>.

* Findings

* Intact <u>urethra</u>: no urethral extravasation with contrast in <u>bladder</u>

* Partial urethral disruption: urethral extravasation with contrast in <u>bladder</u>

* Complete urethral disruption: urethral extravasation and no contrast in <u>bladder</u>

* Complications: <u>UTI</u>





![Retrograde urethrogram with urethral stricture](media/mbno0pnyrcpz7rzcagperepq.jpg)

Retrograde urethrogram with urethral stricture




### Retrograde cystography [[12]](/library/3wYSir)[[13]](/library/Ev18bQ0)




* Description: an imaging modality in which contrast is injected into the <u>bladder</u> via a catheter to inspect <u>bladder</u> anatomy and assess for abnormalities via <u>x-ray</u>

* Indications: suspected <u>bladder injury</u>, e.g., traumatic or <u>iatrogenic</u> injury

* Contraindications: suspected <u>urethral injury</u>

* Procedure

* A transurethral catheter is inserted.

* Contrast is injected into the <u>bladder</u>.

* A series of <u>x-rays</u>, including postvoid images, are obtained.

* Findings: contrast extravasation in <u>bladder injuries</u>





![Intraperitoneal bladder rupture](media/aoz5idgi6b4s9t4wkrf11vim.jpg)

Intraperitoneal bladder rupture

![Cystography](media/iqf6qugy0qm55sd0iklw7og5.jpg)

Cystography




### CT retrograde cystography




* Description: imaging modality using <u>computed tomography</u> to visualize the <u>bladder</u> after retrograde filling with contrast agent

* Indication: evaluation of the <u>bladder</u> for postoperative leakage or rupture following trauma

* Procedure: CT after contrast dye is injected into the <u>bladder</u> via the <u>urethra</u>





### Retrograde pyelography




* Description: a diagnostic procedure in which <u>x-rays</u> are taken as a water-soluble contrast agent is injected into the <u>ureter</u> via <u>cystoscopy</u>

* Indication

* Contraindications to IV/<u>CT urography</u>

* Secondary study to confirm or further characterize findings

* Procedure

* Contrast medium is injected into the <u>ureter</u> using a catheter.

* Serial <u>x-rays</u> of areas of interest are taken.

## Cystoscopy

* Description: an endoscopic procedure in which a thin tube with a light and a camera is inserted through the <u>urethra</u> into the <u>bladder</u>, allowing for visualization of the <u>urethra</u>, <u>bladder</u>, and ureteral orifice

* Indications

* <u>Hematuria</u>

* Suspected <u>interstitial cystitis</u>, gynecological malignancies, <u>endometriosis</u>

* <u>Recurrent urinary tract infections</u>

* <u>Urinary incontinence</u> or <u>overactive bladder</u>

* <u>Urinary tract</u> injuries (traumatic or <u>iatrogenic</u>)

* <u>Urinary obstruction</u>

* Injection of therapeutic drugs (e.g., <u>botulinum toxin</u> for <u>urinary incontinence</u>)

* Procedure: A flexible  or rigid  cystoscope is inserted into the <u>urethra</u> using an <u>electrolyte</u>-containing <u>irrigation</u> fluid or sterile water.

* Complications

* Postprocedural <u>hematuria</u> and/or <u>dysuria</u>

* <u>Urinary tract infection</u>

* <u>Iatrogenic</u> <u>injury to the urethra</u> or <u>bladder</u>





![Cystoscopy](media/hrm3gq7s4wmtl4zx8ueijv42.jpg)

Cystoscopy

## Urinary drainage procedures

### Bladder catheterization [[12]](/library/3wYSir)




* Description: placement of a catheter into the <u>bladder</u> via the <u>urethra</u> or percutaneously through the suprapubic abdominal wall

* Indications

* Sterile urine sample collection

* Measurement of urinary output and/or <u>PVR</u>

* <u>Bladder</u> drainage, e.g., for <u>urinary retention</u>; , <u>urinary obstruction</u>, patients with impaired mobility

* Access for intravesical therapy, e.g., <u>bladder irrigation</u>, <u>chemotherapy</u>

* Urological studies, e.g., cystography

* Types of <u>bladder catheterization</u>

* <u>Transurethral catheterization</u> (e.g., with a <u>Foley catheter</u>)

* <u>Suprapubic catheterization</u>





> [!WARNING]
> <u>Urethral injury</u> (known or suspected) and <u>acute bacterial prostatitis</u> are <u>relative contraindications</u> for <u>transurethral catheterization</u>.

#### Suprapubic catheterization [[12]](/library/3wYSir)




* Description: : a surgical procedure in which a catheter is inserted into the <u>bladder</u> through an <u>incision</u> in the abdominal wall above the <u>pubic symphysis</u>

* Techniques

* Open cystostomy

* Percutaneous cystostomy

* Indications

* Unsuccessful <u>transurethral catheterization</u>, e.g., secondary to <u>urethral strictures</u>, benign <u>prostate</u> <u>hyperplasia</u> (<u>BPH</u>)

* Contraindications for <u>transurethral catheterization</u>, e.g., suspected <u>urethral injury</u>, recent urethral <u>surgery</u>, <u>acute bacterial prostatitis</u>

* Need for long-term indwelling <u>bladder</u> catheter

* Contraindications vary by technique and may include:

* Empty or abnormally positioned <u>bladder</u>

* History of <u>bladder</u> <u>irradiation</u> or <u>surgery</u>

* <u>Bladder cancer</u>

* Overlying <u>cellulitis</u>

* <u>Coagulopathy</u>

* Advantages

* More comfortable for the patient and easier to replace than transurethral catheters

* Minimizes risk of urethral trauma and stricture formation

* Reduces <u>incidence</u> of catheter-associated <u>bacteriuria</u>

* Complications

* Intraprocedural: injury to nearby structures, e.g., <u>bowel perforation</u>, vascular injury

* Postprocedural

* Infection, e.g., <u>UTI</u>, wound infection

* Catheter dislodgement resulting in loss of cystostomy tract

### Ureteral stenting [[14]](/library/xd1EHf0)[[15]](/library/pRdLLp0)[[16]](/library/YaWnQP0)




* Description: a urological procedure that involves insertion of a thin, hollow tube into the <u>ureter</u> to enable drainage of fluid from the <u>renal pelvis</u> into the <u>bladder</u>

* Indications [[16]](/library/YaWnQP0)

* <u>Upper urinary tract obstruction</u> (e.g., <u>nephrolithiasis</u>, tumors, <u>pregnancy</u>)

* <u>Ureteral injuries</u> or <u>fistulas</u> with urinary leakage

* Prevention of <u>ureteral obstruction</u> from passing stone fragments after <u>lithotripsy</u>

* Contraindications [[16]](/library/YaWnQP0)

* Urinary <u>bladder outlet obstruction</u> (e.g., due to <u>BPH</u>) or <u>urinary tract infection</u>

* Uncorrectable <u>coagulopathy</u>

* Procedure

* Insertion of a <u>double-J stent</u> into the <u>ureter</u>

* <u>Cystoscopy</u>-guided transurethral (retrograde) placement or via percutaneous puncture of the <u>renal pelvis</u> under <u>fluoroscopic</u> guidance (antegrade)

* <u>Stent</u> should be exchanged every 3–6 months

* Complications 

* <u>Ureteral injury</u>

* <u>UTI</u>

* <u>Stent</u> encrustation or displacement





### Percutaneous nephrostomy [[17]](/library/aM0QMg)[[18]](/library/aaWQQP0)




* Description: a urological procedure that involves the insertion of a <u>pigtail catheter</u> (nephrostomy tube) into the dilated <u>renal pelvis</u>

* Indications [[18]](/library/aaWQQP0)

* <u>Upper urinary tract obstruction</u> (if <u>ureteral stent</u> cannot be placed)

* <u>Ureteral injuries</u> or <u>fistulas</u>

* Access for urological procedures (e.g., <u>percutaneous nephrolithotomy</u>, delivery of <u>chemotherapeutic agents</u>)

* <u>Antegrade pyelography</u>

* Contraindications: uncorrectable <u>coagulopathy</u> [[18]](/library/aaWQQP0)

* Procedure

* Insertion of a catheter into the <u>renal pelvis</u> under <u>ultrasound</u> guidance using the <u>Seldinger technique</u>

* Consider preoperative <u>antibiotic prophylaxis</u>.

* Catheter should be exchanged every 3 months.

* Complications

* Damage of adjacent organs

* Vascular injury and hemorrhage

* <u>Bowel perforation</u>

* Pleural complications (e.g., <u>pneumothorax</u>, <u>hemothorax</u>)

* <u>Urosepsis</u> (especially in patients with <u>pyonephrosis</u>)

* Catheter encrustation or displacement
